approachQuestion.prompt:
Distance-weighted ledger. A fixed read-only array a has n signed entries. Each of q inclusive requests [l,r] asks for a[l] + 2*a[l+1] + ... + (r-l+1)*a[r]. Return the q answers in request order; weights restart at 1 for every request.

Input: a=[4,-2,5,1], requests [[1,3],[0,1]]. Output: [11,0]. The first total is -2 + 2*5 + 3*1.

Constraints: 1 ≤ n,q ≤ 200000; -1000 ≤ a[i] ≤ 1000. Every request has 0 ≤ l ≤ r < n, with zero-based indices. No updates occur. All intermediate totals and answers fit signed 64-bit integers.

Which approach handles the complete task correctly and efficiently?

options.text: Build P[k]=sum of a[i] for i<k and W[k]=sum of (i+1)*a[i] for i<k, both starting at zero. Return W[r+1]-W[l] - l*(P[r+1]-P[l]).
options.feedback: Global weight i+1 becomes local weight i-l+1 after subtracting l copies of the unweighted range total.

options.text: Build W of globally weighted totals and return W[r+1]-W[l].
options.feedback: Weights must restart at l. For a=[4,-2,5,1] and [1,3], global weights give 15 instead of 11.

options.text: Build ordinary cumulative totals and return (r-l+1)*(P[r+1]-P[l]).
options.feedback: This gives every entry the same weight. For [1,2] on a=[1,2,3], it returns 10 instead of 8.

options.text: For each request walk its positions, multiply by successive weights starting at 1, and add.
options.feedback: This computes the right value but repeats the weighting work for every overlapping request. Two reusable summaries remove those repeated traversals.

feedback.reason: Build both ordinary cumulative totals and totals weighted by the global one-based index. Obtain each range from both summaries. Subtract the left index times its unweighted total from its globally weighted total to restart weights at one.
details: Build both ordinary cumulative totals and totals weighted by the global one-based index. Obtain each range from both summaries. Subtract the left index times its unweighted total from its globally weighted total to restart weights at one.

Global weights at indices left..right are left+1..right+1. Subtract left times the ordinary range sum to change them into local weights 1..length. One unweighted summary cannot recover this distance-weighted total.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the method in the reveal. Choose its tightest worst-case time and worst-case auxiliary-space pair. 64-bit addition, subtraction, multiplication and indexing take constant time. Include both allocated summaries; exclude input arrays and the required q-answer output.

options.text: O(n + q) time; O(n) auxiliary space
O(n + q) time; O(1) auxiliary space
O(n log n + q) time; O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Two prepared arrays answer each weighted request with fixed arithmetic.
details: Two arrays are built in one pass; each answer uses a fixed number of arithmetic operations and array accesses.
64-bit addition, subtraction, multiplication and indexing take constant time. Include both allocated summaries; exclude input arrays and the required q-answer output.
Two n+1 arrays require O(n) space. The iterative method uses constant loop state, no recursion, and no copy of a or the requests.
Direct weighting requires O(nq) worst-case time with O(1) working space. A single globally weighted summary fails when l is nonzero; a single unweighted total loses positional information.

methodReveal.title: Shift global weights to the requested origin
methodReveal.description: Build both ordinary cumulative totals and totals weighted by the global one-based index. Obtain each range from both summaries. Subtract the left index times its unweighted total from its globally weighted total to restart weights at one.
